extracted.intended_audience: Federal land managers (FLMs); State permitting authorities; potential permit applicants; agency staff (FWS, NPS, USFS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Federal land managers on how to consider temporary emissions from overall low-emitting facilities when evaluating effects on Air Quality Related Values (AQRVs) in Federal Class I areas, and how that consideration relates to permitting analyses and statutory roles. Includes scope, alignment with permitting practice, legal consistency, and administrative procedures for finalizing the addendum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual consideration for temporary emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The addendum adds a contextual consideration provision concerning the analysis by Federal land managers (FLMs) of temporary emissions for overall low-emitting facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft/final addendum "adds a contextual criterion for temporary air emissions that would occur alongside any considerations of generally accepted practices for emissions, modeling, and analysis." The purpose is to describe how FLMs will consider temporary emissions for low-emitting facilities when analyzing effects to AQRVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with air permitting analysis / generally accepted engineering practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The FLM analysis should align with the air permitting analysis to the extent the analysis provides information relevant to AQRVs at the potentially impacted Class I area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The addendum does not modify FLAG language regarding general engineering practices; instead, it acknowledges that FLM analysis should align with permitting analysis where that analysis provides relevant information. Temporary-emissions consideration is to be applied alongside generally accepted practices for emissions, modeling, and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Clean Air Act and EPA regulations; preserve permit authority roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The addendum does not alter a permit authority's process to make reasonable progress determinations under the Regional Haze Rule or New Source Review/Prevention of Significant Deterioration determinations, and it is consistent with existing regulations because it applies only to the FLMs' discretionary determinations authorized under the Clean Air Act and implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FLMs' contextual considerations are separate from, and do not supersede, permit authorities' statutory/regulatory roles. The addendum clarifies that temporary-emissions criteria do not conflict with EPA guidance on State reasonable-progress determinations and do not introduce 'extra-regulatory' factors that would change permit processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FLM best professional judgment tied to statutory mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: FLMs should use these criteria to evaluate the effect a project may have on AQRVs in a Class I area and how any predicted AQRV impacts may affect the FLM's ability to manage public lands consistent with statutory mandates (e.g., resource protection and visitor experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The addendum affirms the FLM's discretionary role and responsibility under the Clean Air Act; FLMs apply their best professional judgment in assessing AQRV impacts and management implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollutants and effects to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: The FLAG effort and the addendum focus on pollutants that could affect the health and status of resources in managed areas, primarily ozone, particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrates, and sulfates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should consider these listed pollutants when assessing potential effects to AQRVs in Class I areas; temporary-emission considerations are applied in the context of these pollutant effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability scope — temporary emissions from overall low-emitting facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The addendum specifically addresses how FLMs should consider temporary emission increases associated with overall low-emitting facilities when analyzing effects to AQRVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final addendum is intended to help FLAG 2010 report users understand how FLMs will consider temporary emissions for overall low-emitting facilities; it clarifies that this is a contextual consideration within FLM analyses and does not change regulatory roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative process: consideration of public comments and periodic evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies reviewed and considered comments received on the draft addendum prior to finalizing it; the addendum does not include a sunset date but will be periodically evaluated by FWS in coordination with NPS and USFS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agencies responded to commenters' concerns (e.g., alignment with permitting practice, regulatory consistency, sunset date). Although the addendum has no fixed termination date, agencies will periodically reassess whether it continues to articulate appropriate FLM contextual considerations.
